title: Samsung's LittleBit squeezes AI models to a tenth of a bit per weight
key_facts: Samsung Research's LittleBit method compresses model weights to about 0.1 bit each, a nearly 31x memory cut.
Llama2-13B fits under 0.9GB and Llama2-70B under 2GB, per the team's paper presented as a NeurIPS 2025 poster in December (2025).
On Llama2-7B at 0.1 bits it outperforms competing methods at 0.7 bits, per the team's benchmarks.
Samsung claims up to an 11.6x inference speedup over FP16; code is public on GitHub; a LittleBit-2 successor was tied to ICML 2026.
Samsung has not said whether it will ship in products; public materials call it research.
The article sets it beside PrismML, a Caltech spinout whose compressed Bonsai 27B runs on an iPhone and which CNBC reports is in early talks with Apple.
Google's TurboQuant compresses the key-value cache and moved memory stocks when announced in March.
quote_evidence: Samsung Research says its LittleBit technique can shrink a 13-billion-parameter model to under a gigabyte, at a compression level most quantization methods can't survive without breaking the model.
Samsung also says the compressed format unlocks up to an 11.6x inference speedup over FP16.
Samsung hasn't said whether LittleBit is headed into its own phones or Galaxy Watch lineup, and the company's public materials describe it as a research contribution rather than a shipping product.
why_it_matters_hint: Extreme compression could let capable models run on phones, but this is research from last December.
notes: Older research re-dated: the paper was presented in December 2025; the 8 Oct article is a roundup. Figures are Samsung's own.
